t: In front of you, at the north end of Bloomsbury Square, is the statue of Charles James Fox. Put up in 1816 and made by the sculptor Richard Westmacott, it shows Fox dressed as a Roman senator. Fox was a Whig statesman who died in 1806, after a parliamentary career of thirty-eight years. He was the great rival of the Tory William Pitt the Younger, just as his father had been a rival of Pitt's father. The statue is Grade II star listed.
